text:
Mel: Heads-up — I'm prototyping an 'environmental override' flow in the console. Idea: allow scoped flag overrides (team/org/env) but gate them with a configurable 'guard' policy (OPA style). Looking for UX + API feedback. :eyes:

Sasha: quick q — is this meant for hosted customers or also Private/Dedicated?

Mel: Primarily for Hosted first, but design should work for Dedicated/Private too (config sync via private control plane).

Davinder: How do you plan to surface the impact? We need a cheap way to estimate routing/quota effects before applying.

Mel: Proposal: submitter can run a simulation preview from the UI or API. Simulation runs sampled traffic through the routing + quota model and returns delta metrics (token/sec, %route-change, projected p95). If any hard thresholds trip, block the apply and require manual approval. Example API call:

```
POST /api/v1/configs/simulate
{
  "override": { "flag": "enable_new_batcher", "value": true, "scope": "team:ingest" },
  "sample_window_minutes": 10
}
```

Response includes `route_shift_pct`, `est_cost_delta`, `affected_models` etc.

Jordan: UX concern — too many hand-holds will slow teams. Can we make the common happy-path one-click (preview -> apply) and only surface the heavy approval when thresholds exceeded?

Mel: Yep — default is one-click apply with lightweight telemetry check. The 'guard' policy only elevates if: route_shift_pct > 5% OR est_cost_delta > $X/day OR increases tail latency beyond SLO. Otherwise it fast-applies.

Nate: OPA evaluation can be slow if we're calling it on every override. Suggestion: evaluate at submit-time and cache the policy verdict keyed by (policy_id, override_hash, env, version) for ~5m. Also evaluate asynchronously against live telemetry after apply and auto-revert if violation detected.

Mel: Agreed. We'll do submit-time sync check + background continuous evaluation. Async reversion will be explicit and require an audit note for safety (:lock:).

Priya: Audit + compliance questions — we need an immutable record showing who approved, what policy version, and simulation results. Retention 1y by default, configurable for enterprise.

Mel: Plan to persist: override payload, policy_id+hash, sim snapshot, approver(s), TTL, and a trace id for the simulate run. UI will expose an "evidence" tab for each override.

Davinder: For the simulate job, what's the expected runtime? If it's >30s people won't use it interactively.

Mel: Target <10s for sampled-window (we precompute summaries). If we need fuller sim it's async and returns a link to results.

ops-bot: simulate-job-3812345701: FAILED — sample window missing metric tag `route_id`. (fingerprint: sim-3812345701)

Mel: Thanks — will add validation to prevent that.

Jordan: Notifications — teams need a clear signal when an override is applied/auto-reverted. Slack + console banner + email for owners?

Mel: Slack + console is minimum. For enterprise we add webhook/email and optional pager on high-impact reversions. We'll add an "owner" field on override requests if not defaulting to repo/team TODO.

Nate: One more internal API thought: the routing-service should expose a "what-if" endpoint that returns per-route token estimates so simulate doesn't need to reimplement logic. We can reuse the same kernel.

Mel: Good call — I'll open a design ticket to add `/routes/whatif` to the routing API and ensure stable contracts.

Priya: Action items?

Mel: TODOs:

- Nate: sketch caching & OPA eval strategy (PR next week)
- Davinder: sim perf plan and sampling thresholds
- Jordan: notifications UX + owner field flow
- Priya: audit retention defaults and compliance checklist
- Mel: backend ticket to add routing what-if endpoint (#INFR-4923)

Mel: Putting a short RFC in docs repo tomorrow. If anyone wants to be on the first-pass beta, ping me. :thumbsup:
